title: Students at 100+ Colorado Schools Walk Out Against ICE Presence
detail: Students at more than 100 Colorado middle and high schools — including in Denver, Aurora, Fort Collins, Colorado Springs, Pueblo, Grand Junction, Alamosa, and Nederland — walked out of class at noon on September 4, 2026 to protest ICE's presence near schools and communities under the banner 'Students Say ICE Out.' The walkout was organized by the Colorado Youth Coalition, co-founded by 16-year-old Bre Kennedy of Grandview High School in Aurora, with backing from General Strike US, Brown Berets de Tepetlán, Pulse Colorado, Denver People's March, 50501 Colorado, and No Concentration Camps in Colorado. Denver-area students rallied afterward at La Alma-Lincoln Park. Organizers linked the action to the administration's earlier rollback of 'sensitive locations' guidance that had restricted ICE arrests at schools, hospitals, and places of worship; Kennedy said young people 'are not willing to sit back while communities are harmed and adults in power fail to act.'

title: ICE Agents Baton-Charge Protesters After 40-Hour Stakeout in Frederick, Maryland Neighborhood
detail: ICE agents staked out the Taskers Chance neighborhood of Frederick, Maryland starting at 6 a.m. Thursday, September 3, 2026, after a man fled a traffic stop, remaining on scene for about 40 hours. Protesters gathered the same day and, by Friday evening, September 4, had linked arms to form a 'human barrier' in the street in front of the house under surveillance. At about 9:30 p.m. Friday, agents charged the barrier and struck residents and protesters with batons; video captured an agent pointing a firearm at people on the ground and agents telling residents 'We see you,' 'we know where you live,' and 'we have your license plate.' City Council President César Díaz said a couple of people were injured, though the severity was unclear; no arrests were reported and agents left the neighborhood soon after. Rep. April McClain Delaney, whose district includes Frederick, said she was 'especially disturbed by reports that ICE agents used force against Frederick residents,' and local officials, including Díaz, publicly asked whether the confrontation represented 'the new normal.'
